stories.headline: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wins fourth term as President of Brazil
stories.body:
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won a fourth term as President of Brazil. He defeated Flávio Bolsonaro in the election runoff. Lula won the runoff vote with 51.79% of the total vote. He defeated Flávio Bolsonaro by 4.4 million votes.

Flávio Bolsonaro had won the first round of voting on October 4. He received 47% of the vote in that round. Lula received 45% in the first round.

Brazil's Supreme Court ordered voting hours extended nationwide by two hours on Sunday. Both presidential campaigns requested this extension. Lula's campaign asked for extended hours because of bus transportation issues in nine states. Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign cited heavy rain in southern Brazil. Supreme Electoral Court President Kássio Nunes Marques confirmed Lula's victory. He said the voting time extension did not change the outcome of the race.

US President Donald Trump claimed without providing evidence that Brazil's election looked rigged. Trump also criticized the decision to extend voting hours. Flávio Bolsonaro's political party issued a statement. The party recognized the presidential result announced by the electoral court. But the party called for political debate on questions raised during the election.

Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes banned Flávio Bolsonaro from leaving Brazil. Flávio Bolsonaro is a 45-year-old senator. Justice Moraes ordered him to give up his passports within 24 hours. This Supreme Court ruling relates to a criminal investigation. The investigation involves alleged money laundering with lawyer Willer Tomaz and betting companies.

Flávio Bolsonaro said federal police gave him the travel ban order in Brasília. Police served the order outside the home of his father, Jair Bolsonaro. Former President Jair Bolsonaro is currently under house arrest. He is serving a 27-year prison sentence. He was convicted for plotting a coup after his 2022 election loss.

The election result was unexpected. After the result, the São Paulo stock exchange opened 15% lower. The stock exchange later partially recovered.

claims.text: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won a fourth term as President of Brazil, defeating Flávio Bolsonaro in the election runoff.
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won the runoff vote with 51.79% of the total, defeating Flávio Bolsonaro by 4.4 million votes.
Flávio Bolsonaro had won the first round of voting on October 4 with 47% of the vote, ahead of Lula's 45%.
Brazil's Supreme Court ordered voting hours extended nationwide by two hours on Sunday following requests from both presidential campaigns.
Lula's campaign requested extended voting hours due to bus transportation issues in nine states, while Bolsonaro's campaign cited heavy rain in southern Brazil.
Supreme Electoral Court President Kássio Nunes Marques confirmed Lula's victory and stated that the voting time extension did not alter the race's outcome.
US President Donald Trump claimed without providing evidence that Brazil's election looked rigged and criticized the decision to extend voting hours.
Flávio Bolsonaro's political party issued a statement recognizing the presidential result proclaimed by the electoral court while calling for political debate on raised questions.
Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes banned 45-year-old senator Flávio Bolsonaro from leaving Brazil and ordered him to surrender his passports within 24 hours.

The Supreme Court ruling regarding Flávio Bolsonaro's passport relates to a criminal investigation into his alleged involvement in a money-laundering scheme involving lawyer Willer Tomaz and betting companies.
Flávio Bolsonaro stated federal police served him with the travel ban order outside the Brasília residence of his father, Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest.
Former President Jair Bolsonaro is currently serving a 27-year prison sentence following a conviction for plotting a coup after his 2022 election loss.
Following the unexpected election result, the São Paulo stock exchange opened 15% lower before partially recovering.

stories.headline: Student List movement wins majority in Serbia parliamentary election
stories.body:
The opposition Student List movement won Serbia's parliamentary election with 52.45% of the vote. The Student List won 138 seats in the National Assembly. The Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia list received 39.2% of the vote. That list secured 103 seats.

Outgoing President Aleksandar Vučić conceded defeat late on Sunday. His concession ended 14 years of rule by his Serbian Progressive Party. Vučić alleged the election result verified a revolution supported by European countries and the US deep state.

The Student List movement formed after a railway station canopy collapsed in Novi Sad on November 1, 2024. That collapse killed 16 people.

Voter turnout reached 69% as over 4.4 million citizens voted. Turnout was 55.5% in December 2023.

The Student List trained at least 16,000 official controllers and mobile teams. They monitored for fraud like carousel voting and parallel lists.

The movement is leaderless and has no hierarchy. Its candidates include academics, doctors, actors, and farmers without prior political experience. Prominent figures include cardiologist Ilija Srdanović, former central bank governor Dejan Šoškić, and chemistry professor Radomir Saičić.

European Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos said a new chapter can begin for Serbia. She said the European Union door is open. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Russia hopes Serbia's new leadership sees cooperation with Russia as beneficial.

claims.text: In Serbia's parliamentary election, the opposition Student List movement won 52.45% of the vote and 138 seats in the National Assembly.
The Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia list received 39.2% of the vote, securing 103 seats.
Outgoing president Aleksandar Vučić conceded defeat late on Sunday, ending 14 years of rule by his Serbian Progressive Party.
Following his concession, Aleksandar Vučić alleged the election result was the verification of a revolution directly supported by European countries and the US deep state.
The Student List movement emerged following the November 1, 2024 collapse of a railway station canopy in Novi Sad, which killed 16 people.
Voter turnout in Serbia reached 69% with over 4.4 million citizens voting, compared to 55.5% in December 2023.
The Student List trained at least 16,000 official controllers and mobile monitoring teams to detect voter fraud practices like carousel voting and parallel lists.
The Student List movement is non-hierarchical and leaderless, fielding candidates including academics, doctors, actors, and farmers with no prior political experience.
Prominent figures on the Student List include cardiologist Ilija Srdanović, former central bank governor Dejan Šoškić, and chemistry professor Radomir Saičić.
European Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos stated that a new chapter can begin for Serbia and that the EU door is open.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov stated Russia hopes Serbia's new leadership understands that cooperation with Russia is in Serbia's interests.

vocab.meaning: admitted defeat in an election or contest
the percentage or number of people who vote in an election

stories.headline: Israel prepares for national election as West Bank displacements and regional tensions rise
stories.body:
Israel will hold a parliamentary election on October 27 to choose 120 members of the Knesset. A party or coalition needs 61 seats to establish a governing coalition. Polls show Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's far-right coalition trailing an opposition bloc. Retired general Gadi Eisenkot leads that opposition bloc. Neither side is projected to reach 61 seats.

Netanyahu posted an AI-generated image of a nuclear cloud destroying Tel Aviv. He warned voters to elect him or face nuclear destruction from Iran. Israeli media reported a clash between Netanyahu and IDF Chief of Staff Lt Gen Eyal Zamir. Zamir requested a written military directive concerning Iran. Eisenkot said he would not allow the military to become a pawn for Netanyahu's political survival.

Reports indicated Netanyahu tried to persuade US President Donald Trump to attack Iran. But Trump ruled out action until after the US midterm elections.

Israeli forces detained an international delegation of 23 people at the border for nine hours. The group included UK MP Clive Lewis and Scottish MP Lara Bird. Israeli forces barred them from entering the West Bank.

UN rights chief Volker Türk warned of ethnic cleansing after Israeli forces displaced over 3,000 Palestinians in Hebron. The displacement followed a checkpoint attack where two Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers. The UN aid office recorded at least 160 Israeli settler attacks linked to the olive harvest in early October.

claims.text: Israel holds a parliamentary election on October 27 to elect the 120 members of the Knesset, requiring 61 seats to establish a governing coalition.
Polls show Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's far-right coalition trailing the opposition bloc led by retired general Gadi Eisenkot, with neither side projected to reach 61 seats.
Benjamin Netanyahu posted an AI-generated image of a nuclear mushroom cloud destroying Tel Aviv, warning voters to elect him or face nuclear annihilation from Iran.
Israeli media reported a clash between Benjamin Netanyahu and IDF Chief of Staff Lt Gen Eyal Zamir over a military directive concerning Iran that Zamir requested in writing.
Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot stated that he would not allow the IDF to be turned into a pawn in Netanyahu's political survival campaign.
Reports indicated Benjamin Netanyahu tried to persuade US President Donald Trump to launch a renewed assault on Iran, but Trump ruled out action until after the US midterm elections.
Israeli forces detained an international delegation of 23 people, including UK MP Clive Lewis and Scottish MP Lara Bird, at the border for nine hours and barred them from entering the West Bank.
UN rights chief Volker Türk warned of ethnic cleansing concerns after Israeli forces forcibly displaced over 3,000 Palestinians from their homes in Hebron.
Israel's displacement operation in Hebron followed a Friday checkpoint attack near the city in which two Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers.
The UN aid coordination office recorded at least 160 Israeli settler attacks linked to the olive harvest in the first two weeks of October.

a group of people chosen to represent an organization or country

stories.headline: Jordan launches airstrikes in Syria and arrests suspects after church attack
stories.body:
Jordanian security forces arrested three men following a shootout in the city of Karak. The shootout occurred at an abandoned house at dawn. Security forces arrested brothers Hazzah Zaidan Mohammad and Mishal Zaidan Mohammad, alongside Ahmad Sami Hussein. All three suspects were wounded in the shootout. Authorities seized a large cache of munitions.

The arrests followed an attack during a funeral at St George's Church in Hammoud village. Nine people died and over two dozen were wounded in that Friday attack. Public Security chief Maj Gen Obaidallah Abd Rabbo Al-Maayta described the attackers as extremist fighters acting independently. Jordanian Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya said all suspects were Jordanians with no foreign collaboration.

King Abdullah II declared three days of national mourning. He vowed to respond with an iron fist against terrorist ideologies.

The Jordanian air force launched retaliatory airstrikes against armed groups in southern Syria. The health director in Syria's Daraa province reported that at least five civilians died in those strikes. But Syria's SANA news agency quoted the same official saying at least eight civilians were killed.

Eight church attack victims were buried beside the church on Sunday. The ninth victim was buried in south Amman on Monday.

claims.text: Jordanian security forces arrested three Jordanian men—brothers Hazzah Zaidan Mohammad and Mishal Zaidan Mohammad, and Ahmad Sami Hussein—following a dawn shootout at an abandoned house in Karak.
All three suspects were wounded during the shootout with security forces, and a large cache of munitions was seized.
Nine people were killed and over two dozen wounded in a Friday attack during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, Jordan.
The attack took place during a funeral procession at St George's Church in the village of Hammoud, located in Jordan's Karak governorate.
Public Security Directorate chief Maj Gen Obaidallah Abd Rabbo Al-Maayta described the attackers as takfiri extremists who acted independently.
Jordanian Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya stated that the suspects were all Jordanians and there was no indication of foreign collaboration.
Jordan's King Abdullah II declared three days of national mourning and vowed to respond with an iron fist against terrorist ideologies.
The Jordanian air force conducted retaliatory airstrikes against positions of armed groups in southern Syria tied to the Karak attack.
The health director in Syria's Daraa province reported that at least five civilians were killed in the Jordanian airstrikes.
The director of health for Daraa province told Syria's state news agency SANA that at least eight civilians were killed in the Jordanian strikes.
Eight of the Karak church attack victims were buried beside the church on Sunday, while the ninth victim was buried in south Amman on Monday.

vocab.meaning: done in order to pay back or get revenge for an attack

stories.headline: Election Commission defends voter roll revision process in Supreme Court
stories.body:
The Election Commission of India filed an affidavit in the Supreme Court to defend voter roll revisions. Deputy Election Commissioner Bhanu Prakash Yeturu filed the affidavit. He declared that the Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners unanimously decided on June 24, 2025, to conduct a nationwide voter roll revision.

Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and others filed petitions challenging the process. Their challenge followed a news report alleging differences among the commissioners. The Indian Express reported that Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi objected to decisions 14 times.

The Election Commission stated that letters sent by Sandhu and Joshi pertained to internal work allocation. An internal order issued on July 28 was never implemented.

The commission denied amending Form 6 in its revision orders. It noted that only the Central Government can amend Form 6. The new process requires voters to link their details with parents or grandparents in earlier rolls.

Karnataka's final electoral roll will be published on October 27. The state's voter count dropped from 5.54 crore to 4.54 crore after 1.07 crore names were deleted. Opposition parties protested to demand the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

claims.text: The Election Commission filed an affidavit in the Supreme Court stating that the Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners unanimously decided on June 24, 2025, to conduct a nationwide Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

The affidavit was filed by Deputy Election Commissioner Bhanu Prakash Yeturu with the declaration that it was approved by a unanimous decision of the Chief Election Commissioner and the two Election Commissioners.

Petitions filed by opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and others challenged the SIR process following a news report alleging differences between Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.
A report by The Indian Express stated that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections on at least 14 occasions over 10 months regarding SIR decisions.

The Election Commission stated in its affidavit that letters sent by S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi to the cabinet secretary on July 29 pertained to administrative matters and an internal work allocation order.
An internal work allocation office order issued on July 28 was never implemented following a joint direction on July 30 by the two Election Commissioners.
The Election Commission denied in court that Form 6 was amended by its SIR orders issued on June 24, October 27, and May 14.
Form 6 can only be amended by the Central Government, and the declaration introduced by the Election Commission's SIR orders is not a part of Form 6.

The Election Commission clarified to the Supreme Court that a declaration form added under the SIR requires voters to link their details with those of their parents and grandparents in earlier electoral rolls.
Karnataka's final electoral roll under the Special Intensive Revision will be published on October 27.
Karnataka had 5.54 crore voters when the SIR began, and 1.07 crore names were deleted, leaving around 4.54 crore voters on the final roll.
Opposition parties and the Cockroach Janta Party staged protests demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

vocab.meaning: a written statement confirmed by oath for use as evidence in court
a formal written request made to an official body or court

stories.headline: Andhra Pradesh and Odisha prepare emergency response as Cyclone Arnab approaches
stories.body:
The Andhra Pradesh government released ₹27 crore to 20 districts to prepare for Cyclone Arnab. The money will support relief operations ahead of the cyclone's expected landfall on October 28.

The India Meteorological Department forecast that Cyclone Arnab will cross the coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam. The cyclone will also affect the Yanam coast. Winds are expected to reach sustained speeds of 115 to 125 kilometers per hour. Wind gusts could reach up to 140 kilometers per hour.

At 5:30 am on October 26, Cyclone Arnab was 590 kilometers northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram. It was 610 kilometers southeast of Gopalpur. The storm was also 650 kilometers east-southeast of Visakhapatnam.

Officials in Andhra Pradesh scheduled 4,711 pregnant women to move to safer healthcare facilities. A total of 30,043 fishing boats returned to harbours across the state.

The Andhra Pradesh Department of Health prepared 6,431 emergency beds for the storm. The department readied 630 medical teams and 716 vehicles. Health authorities also stocked 13,101 doses of anti-snake venom across facilities.

The Real Time Governance Society urged residents to report emergencies through WhatsApp. Residents can use the Mana Mitra platform for cyclone help.

State Disaster Management Authority Director Prakhar Jain reported that 7 NDRF teams and 8 SDRF teams deployed to vulnerable districts. Fifteen NDRF teams deployed across vulnerable locations in Andhra Pradesh and Puducherry's Yanam district.

In New Delhi, Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan chaired a National Crisis Management Committee meeting. The committee reviewed cyclone preparedness across several states.

The Andaman and Nicobar Islands ordered all schools to close until Tuesday. The Odisha government ordered schools, colleges, and Anganwadi centres to close on October 28 and 29 in six southern districts.

Odisha Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh Prabhakar Patil said 135 cyclone shelters were prepared. The state also prepared 1,600 temporary accommodation centres. Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Majhi assigned eight state ministers to monitor preparations in different locations.
